s.d: literally: to arise; hence: = process by which humans leave a position of relative obscurity and enter the public arena
s.g: to arise; to appear; to come

s.d: literally: to cause to arise; hence: = causative action by which humans put a construction in place
s.g: to raise; to erect; to set up; to put together; to build

s.d: literally: to raise up; hence: = causative process by which deities cause humans to leave a position of relative obscurity and enter the public arena
s.g: to raise up; to bring into existence

s.d: literally: to raise up; hence: = causative action by which deities bring objects into existence
literally: to raise up seed; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities make sure that people have descendents
literally: to establish (people) as (one's special) people; hence: = action by which deities associate themselves with a certain group of people and establish a special relationship with them
literally: to arise (against someone); hence: = action by which humans or animals approach (other) humans with the intention of opposing or fighting them
s.g: to rise up (against); to oppose; to attack

s.d: literally: to raise up (humans against humans); hence: = causative action by which a deity causes humans to approach other humans with the intention of opposing or fighting them
literally: attacker; hence: = a person who has initiated a conflict with someone else and acts accordingly
literally: to raise (from a low position); hence: = causative process by with deities cause humans to gain a higher status within the society
literally: to arise; hence: = process by which an event starts taking place
s.g: to arise; to happen; to come

s.d: literally: to raise; hence: = causative action by which deities establish a certain condition
s.g: to arise; to happen; to come

s.d: literally: to cause (words or plans) to stand; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities cause plans or promises to be carried out as intended
literally: (a condition) arises; hence: = process by which an event grows in intensity

literally: to rise up over the name (of someone else); hence: = process by which humans start bearing the name of other humans, even though they are not their direct biological offspring, ◄ as a result of levirate marriage
s.g: to assume the name (of someone else)

s.d: literally: to rise (and move to someone else); hence: = process by which a property is transferred from one owner to another
state or process by which objects or substances have or assume an upright shape

literally: to cause to arise; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities put an object in an upright position, which can consist of either a single object like a stone or a collection of objects that form a single unit
literally: to arise; hence: = action by which humans or deities position themselves in a standing position in a certain location
literally: to stand; hence: = state in which humans live through an experience without being affected
literally: to cause to stand; hence: = causative action by which humans assign roles and responsibilities to other humans
literally: to stand; hence: = state in which an object remains firmly standing in its place
literally: to hold; hence: = process by which a certain condition endures for an extended time
s.g: to stand; to remain; to endure

s.d: literally: to cause to hold; hence: = causative action by which deities cause a certain condition to endure for an extended time
s.g: to make stand; to establish; to cause to endure

s.d: literally: to endure; hence: = state in which humans stand by a certain principle
literally: to cause to stand; hence: = causative action by which deities provide comfort to people who are grieving
literally: to stand; hence: = state in which humans have sufficient physical or military strength to withstand attacks by others
s.g: to stand firm; to hold (one's) ground

s.d: literally: to cause to stand; hence: = causative action by which deities cause humans to have sufficient physical or military strength to withstand attacks by others
s.g: to cause to stand firm; to support

s.d: literally: to stand; hence: = process by which humans can complete a certain activity successfully
s.g: to be effective; to avail; to succeed

s.d: literally: to cause to stand; hence: = causative action by which someone in authority confirms the truth and authority of what has been communicated
literally: to cause a covenant to stand; hence: = action by which a deity proposes a solemn agreement with another party, accompanied by stipulations, blessings, and curses
literally: (one's) eyes stand; hence: = state in which the human eyes are no longer able to see and are fixed in one direction
literally: to arise; hence: = process by which a sick or wounded person regains the ability to stand up and walk
literally: to raise up; hence: = causative process by which a deity causes a sick or wounded person to regain the ability to stand up and walk
literally: to raise up (someone who is stumbling); hence: = causative action by which deities give inner strength to humans who are about to fail in their efforts
literally: to arise; hence: = action by which humans reject the authority of a ruler to which they had formerly been subjected
literally: to cause to arise; hence: = causative action by which humans cause other humans to reject the authority of a ruler to which they had formerly been subjected
s.g: to cause to rebel; to stir up (against)

s.d: vertical height of an object
state in which humans stand or walk in an upright position; ≈ associated with confidence and pride
ethnic group ◄ located in Mesopotamia; living east of the Tigris

large primate with long tail and doglike muzzle, the size of a fairly large dog; usually light brown in color, but older males sometimes turn gray; some large males develop a mane like a lion; they spend most of their time on the ground and eat a variety of roots, shoots, fruits, leaves, insects, and small reptiles; ◄ various subspecies of |ipapio|i*; ► brought to Israel from Tarsis
process by which humans and deities experience an emotion of strong disapproval and rejection of a person or situation
s.g: to abhor; to detest; to resent; to reject; to oppose; to be hostile

s.d: process by which human experience an emotion of fear ◄ regarding someone who is more powerful or numerous
meaning unsure; possibly: = causative action by which humans cause other humans to fear
small shrub with thorns; ≈ associated with things of no value, aggression, and destruction
man; ◄ tribe of {L:Judah<SDBH:יְהוּדָה>}; ► father of {L:Anub<SDBH:עָנוּב>} and {L:Zobebah<SDBH:צֹבֵבָה>}
long locks of hair; ≈ associated with masculine beauty
causative action by which humans dig a well
causative action by which humans strike an object or person repeatedly with hard blows ► in order to destroy or kill it
s.g: to batter; to knock down; to beat down

s.d: causative action by which objects cause other objects to stay cool and fresh
s.g: to keep cool; to keep fresh

s.d: literally: to keep cool and fresh; hence: = causative action by which humans make sure that an event continues to be performed well
woven fabric of fine threads,◄ made by spiders ► to trap insects
length of cut timber ◄ cut from a tree; ► used for the construction of a building
length of wood ► supporting the roof of a building
literally: beam, rafter; hence: = covering of a house ◄ normally supported by beams and rafters; ≈ associated with shade and security
action by which someone places a trap ► in order to catch an animal; ≈ associated with aggression and control
man, also known as {L:Kishi<SDBH:קִישִׁי>}; ◄ tribe of {L:Levi<SDBH:לֵוִי>}; ► father of {L:Ethan<SDBH:אֵיתָן>}, a temple singer
a marker indicating that what follows is more limited in duration than expected
event that causes the end of a large number of people
event that causes the end of a large number of people

woman; ◄ concubine of {L:Abraham<SDBH:אַבְרָהָם>}; ► mother of {L:Zimran<SDBH:זִמְרָן>}, {L:Jokshan<SDBH:יָקְשָׁן>}, {L:Medan<SDBH:מְדָן>}, {L:Midian<SDBH:מִדְיָן>}, {L:Ishbak<SDBH:יִשְׁבָּק>}, and {L:Shuah<SDBH:שׁוּחַ>}
smoke ◄ produced by burning sacrifice or incense ► in order to please God with its smell
s.g: smoke (from incense burned as sacrifice to God)

s.d: causative action by which humans or deities cause people or animals to die
causative action by which humans or deities cause people to die
causative action by which humans reduce the size of an inanimate
literally: to be smaller than an event; hence: = state in which humans consider themselves unworthy of something
s.g: to be unworthy of; to not deserve

s.d: state in which an event is considered trivial and insignificant
s.g: to be small; to be trivial; to be insignificant

s.d: state in which animate or inanimate objects are relatively small in size, ≈ which is sometimes associated with a lack of strength, and with insignificance
state in which humans are relatively young, ≈ which is associated with being insignificant, but also with being healthy
state in which humans are of relatively low esteem
state in which an event is considered trivial and insignificant

state in which animate or inanimate objects are relatively small in size
state in which humans are relatively young, ≈ which is sometimes associated with being weak and inexperienced, but also with being healthy
state in which humans are of relatively low esteem
state in which an event is considered trivial and insignificant
state in which a case is considered relatively easy to solve
state in which an event is of short duration
the smallest of the fingers of a human hand; ≈ regarded as relatively insignificant
causative action by which humans remove leaves, branches, fruits, or the entire stalk of a plant
action by which humans or animals empty their stomachs of its contents; ◄ after having eaten too much, having ingested contaminated food, or due to sickness or excessive alcohol consumption
action by which humans or animals vomit up something specific from their stomachs
literally: to vomit; hence: = process by which humans lose their possessions in an unpleasant way
s.g: to vomit > lose (one's wealth as punishment)

s.d: literally: to vomit; hence: = causative action by which land refuses to allow people to remain as if they were contaminated food
s.g: to vomit > to expel (its people because of their sin)

s.d: to sing a song in which one expresses one's grief at the loss of a loved one or the destruction of a town or nation
s.g: to lament; to mourn; to bewail in a song

s.d: to sing a {L:song<SDBH:קִינָה>} in which one expresses one's grief at the loss of a loved one or the destruction of a town or nation
s.g: to sing a dirge; to lament; to mourn; to bewail in a song

s.d: female person who is skillful at wailing and has made it her profession
process by which humans open their eyes after sleep; ≈ also used in the figurative sense of becoming active after a period of inactivity, and of being restored to life after having died
literally: to wake up, but extended to events: = process by which an event starts happening
action by which an animal spends the season of {L:summer<SDBH:קַיִץ>} engaged in a certain activity
process by which humans open their eyes after sleep; ≈ also used in the figurative sense of becoming active after a period of inactivity, and of being restored to life after having died
literally: to wake up, but extended to events: = process by which an event starts happening
action by which an animal spends the season of {L:summer<SDBH:קַיִץ>} engaged in a certain activity

type of partridge, of which there were at least three variaties in ancient Israel;  it lives in small flocks called coveys, lays a great many eggs, and prefers to run when in danger, flying only when necessary; even when it takes flight it flies for only a short distance before dropping back to the ground; habitat differs from one kind of partridge to another; the rock partridge is about 35 centimeters (14 inches) in length and has striking white cheeks with a black band running from its brow, through its eyes, down its neck, and curving around its breast; It also has striking black and chestnut stripes on its flanks; its back and wings are gray; the beak and legs are red; both sexes look alike; the black francolin is about the same size but has a slightly shorter tail; the male has a black breast and flanks; the female is a speckled brown; the sand partridge is the color of the local sand and is about half the size of the other two types; ◄ Alectoris graeca, Alectoris chukar, Francolinus francolinus, Ammoperdix heyi; ► clean animal, so may be eaten
s.g: rock partridge; black francolin; sand partridge

s.d: man; ◄ son of {L:Ebiasaph<SDBH:אֶבְיָסָף>}; tribe of {L:Levi<SDBH:לֵוִי>}; ► father of {L:Shallum<SDBH:שַׁלּוּם>}, gatekeeper, after exile
man; ◄ descendant of {L:Asaph<SDBH:אָסָף>}; tribe of {L:Levi<SDBH:לֵוִי>}; ► gatekeeper; time of king {L:David<SDBH:דָּוִד>}
man; ◄ son of {L:Jimnah<SDBH:יִמְנָה>}; tribe of {L:Levi<SDBH:לֵוִי>}; ► gatekeeper; time of king {L:Hezekiah<SDBH:חִזְקִיָּהוּ>}
